question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A wet blanket

options.text: A person who loves the rain
A person who spoils the enjoyment of others

explanation: A wet blanket = उत्साह ठंडा करने वाला व्यक्ति। Example: Don't be a wet blanket; join the party.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To ride roughshod over

options.text: To treat others harshly, ignoring their feelings

explanation: Ride roughshod over = बेरहमी से कुचलना, परवाह न करना। Example: The builder rode roughshod over the villagers' objections.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To fight shy of

options.text: To avoid something out of reluctance

explanation: Fight shy of = कतराना, बचना। Example: He fights shy of public speaking.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pull the wool over someone's eyes
explanation: Pull the wool over someone's eyes = आँखों में धूल झोंकना। Example: The agent pulled the wool over the buyer's eyes.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To split hairs

options.text: To argue over tiny, unimportant differences

explanation: Split hairs = बाल की खाल निकालना। Example: Stop splitting hairs and accept the offer.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pay lip service

options.text: To express support in words without acting on it

explanation: Pay lip service = सिर्फ़ ज़ुबानी समर्थन जताना। Example: Many leaders only pay lip service to women's safety.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To have a field day

options.text: To enjoy a time of great success or opportunity
To spend a day in a field
To have a very bad day

explanation: Have a field day = मौक़े का भरपूर मज़ा या फ़ायदा उठाना। Example: Reporters had a field day with the minister's blunder.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To lick one's wounds

options.text: To recover quietly after a defeat
To treat a wound with medicine

explanation: Lick one's wounds = हार के बाद चुपचाप सँभलना। Example: The team went home to lick their wounds.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To rub salt into the wound

options.text: To make someone's pain or distress worse

explanation: Rub salt into the wound = जले पर नमक छिड़कना। Example: Laughing at his failure was rubbing salt into the wound.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To sow one's wild oats

options.text: To work hard on a farm
To grow crops in a hurry
To behave recklessly in one's youth
To save money for old age

explanation: Sow one's wild oats = जवानी में लापरवाह मौज-मस्ती करना। Example: He sowed his wild oats before settling down.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To tilt at windmills

options.text: To work in a flour mill

explanation: Tilt at windmills = काल्पनिक शत्रुओं से लड़ना। Example: Fighting a non-existent rule is tilting at windmills.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To run the gauntlet

options.text: To face a series of attacks or hostile criticism

explanation: Run the gauntlet = आलोचनाओं या हमलों की बौछार झेलना। Example: The witness had to run the gauntlet of angry reporters.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To turn turtle

options.text: To capsize or turn upside down

explanation: Turn turtle = उलट जाना, पलट जाना। Example: The boat turned turtle in the storm.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To live from hand to mouth

options.text: To spend all one earns just to survive
To live a life of luxury

explanation: Live from hand to mouth = रोज़ कमाकर रोज़ खाना। Example: Daily wagers often live from hand to mouth.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To bury one's head in the sand
explanation: Bury one's head in the sand = ख़तरे से आँखें मूँद लेना। Example: Burying your head in the sand will not clear the debts.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To play fast and loose

options.text: To take part in a sport
To behave carelessly and without a sense of responsibility
To play a game very quickly
To lose a game on purpose

explanation: Play fast and loose = लापरवाही या बेईमानी से पेश आना। Example: He played fast and loose with the company's funds.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To go to the dogs

options.text: To fall into a bad or ruined condition
To go for a long walk

explanation: Go to the dogs = बर्बाद हो जाना। Example: The firm went to the dogs after the founder died.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To sing for one's supper

options.text: To perform in a music concert
To cook a meal at night
To do some work in return for a favour received

explanation: Sing for one's supper = मिली मदद के बदले कुछ काम करना। Example: The guests had to sing for their supper by washing the dishes.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To make a clean breast of
explanation: Make a clean breast of = सब कुछ साफ़-साफ़ क़बूल कर लेना। Example: The clerk made a clean breast of the theft.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To hold the fort

options.text: To take charge while others are away

explanation: Hold the fort = पीछे से ज़िम्मेदारी सँभालना। Example: Please hold the fort while I attend the meeting.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To go off at a tangent

options.text: To suddenly change from one topic to another
To move in a straight line

explanation: Go off at a tangent = मूल विषय से हटकर अचानक दूसरी बात करने लगना। Example: The speaker went off at a tangent in the middle of the lecture.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To keep a stiff upper lip

options.text: To stay calm and firm in the face of trouble

explanation: Keep a stiff upper lip = मुसीबत में धैर्य बनाए रखना। Example: She kept a stiff upper lip throughout the crisis.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: On tenterhooks

options.text: In a state of anxious suspense
In a state of deep sleep

explanation: On tenterhooks = बेचैनी भरी प्रतीक्षा में। Example: The students were on tenterhooks before the result.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: At loggerheads
explanation: At loggerheads = तीखे मतभेद में। Example: The partners are at loggerheads over the profits.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To throw a spanner in the works

options.text: To spoil a plan by causing trouble

explanation: Throw a spanner in the works = बने-बनाए काम में अड़ंगा डालना। Example: His late objection threw a spanner in the works.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A damp squib

options.text: A small explosion that causes damage
An event that fails to live up to expectations

explanation: A damp squib = उम्मीद से बहुत फीका निकला आयोजन। Example: The much-hyped film turned out to be a damp squib.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A red herring

options.text: Something that misleads or distracts from the real issue

explanation: A red herring = ध्यान भटकाने वाली बात। Example: The missing watch was a red herring in the case.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To nail one's colours to the mast

options.text: To hoist a flag for fun
To declare one's position firmly and refuse to change it

explanation: Nail one's colours to the mast = अपने पक्ष पर डटे रहने की घोषणा करना। Example: The leader nailed his colours to the mast on reforms.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A Trojan horse

options.text: Something that hides a harmful purpose behind a pleasant look

explanation: A Trojan horse = मीठी छुरी, छिपा हुआ ख़तरा। Example: The free software turned out to be a Trojan horse.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A swan song

options.text: A final appearance or farewell performance

explanation: A swan song = अंतिम प्रस्तुति या विदाई-प्रदर्शन। Example: The match was the veteran's swan song.
